newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentines occupying Fiat plant meet officials.
newsitem.headline: Argentines occupying Fiat plant meet officials.

text.p: About 700 Argentine car workers who have occupied a Fiat factory in Cordoba province held talks with local government officials on Sunday, but the firm said its factory was still in workers' hands.
"The plant is still being held, in a totally peaceful way, by about 700 workers," said Fiat spokesman Eduardo Bischoff, quoted by state news agency Telam.
Workers from a car-parts factory who were transferred to Fiat's Ferreyra car plant have occupied the factory for five days, demanding they keep the same pay and conditions.
But Bischoff called their occupation "pressure which gets in the way of negotiations".
Provincial government Labor Secretary Norberto Ciaravino said talks "remain open and positions are close, it's now just a matter of the workers abandoning the factory".

But the local chief of the car workers' union SMATA, Jose Campellone, said the occupation "is for an indefinite period". Unions would stage a major demonstration outside the plant on Thursday, when Argentine trade unions begin a nationwide 36-hour general strike, he said.
